record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and a partial file list only; code and result files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal behavior after applying refusal-direction ablation to Gemma-4-31B-it, but does not specify enough of the original method to establish a direct reproduction.
record.gate_note: The README says the ablated actor had 0% refusals across 500 messages in the paper. The cited original method and the 70% child-likeness result across 100 messages are not separate qualifying findings about refusal.
record.test_reason: The study uses refusal-direction ablation (abliteration of Gemma-4-31B-it, via an external tool) as a tool to build a child-actor model for multi-turn simulations. The only related number is a validation check of that tool: 0% refusals across 500 actor messages, taken from the paper. There is no unablated baseline and no addition or capability test. The messages are child role-play turns, not a harmful/harmless instruction set. This is reporting the performance of the study's own tool, not testing whether the direction mediates refusal.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The README uses refusal-direction ablation (citing Arditi et al.) to build a non-refusing Gemma-4-31B-it child actor, and withholds that checkpoint as safety-sensitive. It tells users to validate a rebuilt actor for refusals and child-likeness: the paper reports 0% refusals across 500 messages and 70% clearly child-like across 100. The paper's actual conclusions concern child-safety benchmarking, not the refusal direction.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes refusal-direction ablation and points to an external implementation, but does not detail how the direction is found or exactly how ablation is performed.
record.peer_reviewed: Findings of EMNLP 2026 (accepted, as stated in README)
record.problems: The refusal-rate result is reported as a paper result in the README; the underlying data and ablation procedure were not inspected. No baseline, uncertainty, or general-capability assessment is given.
record.rows_left_out: No other README-reported result was retained: general benchmark scores and child-likeness validation do not measure the refusal-direction claim.

untested.parts: Ablation vs. unablated baseline on harmful instructions, adding the direction to induce refusal, and preservation of other abilities: none reported.
No baseline refusal rate for unablated Gemma-4-31B-it and no capability check of the abliterated model; only a 0% refusal validation figure on actor messages.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 and its V1 'supports' label are overturned. The study only uses abliteration as an instrument. Its 0% refusal figure is a self-validation with no baseline, from the README rather than the paper body, and the code was not read. Even taken at face value, it would be weak anecdotal consistency with V2, not a test of it.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not report adding the direction, effects on harmless requests, or whether other abilities were preserved.
No result on a weight edit removing refusal in released models.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No test of affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No test of transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
No test of how refusal training affects whether a removable direction exists.
